question: Which one of the following statements for an object falling freely under the influence of gravity is correct?
opt_a: Zero acceleration always implies zero velocity
opt_b: Zero acceleration has no relation with the velocity of the object
opt_c: Zero velocity at any instant necessarily means zero acceleration at that instant
opt_d: Acceleration is constant all throughout the free fall
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Acceleration is constant all throughout the free fall. Free fall means gravity is the only force acting. Newton's second law then gives a = mg/m = g, and the mass cancels out, so every falling body near the Earth's surface picks up speed at the same fixed rate of about 9.8 metres per second every second. The velocity changes from moment to moment; the acceleration producing that change does not.

question: Two magnetic field lines produced by the same source
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, never intersect. A magnetic field line is drawn so that its tangent at every point gives the direction a compass needle would settle into there. Two lines crossing would mean the field had two different directions at the crossing point, and a compass placed there would have to point two ways at once. Since the field at any point has one definite direction, the lines can never meet.

question: Which one of the following statements regarding Fleming's Rule is correct?
opt_a: Fleming's left hand rule gives direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
opt_b: Fleming's right hand rule gives direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
opt_c: Both the left-hand and right-hand rule can be used for finding direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field
opt_d: Fleming's rules has nothing to do with magnetic field
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Fleming's left hand rule gives direction of force on a current-carrying conductor in a magnetic field. The left hand serves the motor effect. Hold the thumb, forefinger and central finger of the left hand mutually at right angles: the forefinger points along the field, the central finger along the current, and the thumb then gives the direction of the force, which is the direction the conductor moves. The right hand rule answers the reverse question: a conductor is moved through a field, and it tells you which way the induced current flows.

question: Which one of the following statements regarding motion is correct?
opt_a: All the periodic motions are necessarily simple harmonic
opt_b: All the simple harmonic motions are necessarily periodic motions
opt_c: There is no co-relation between the simple harmonic motions and the periodicity of motion
opt_d: The relation between the simple harmonic motion and periodic motion depends upon the mass of object undergoing the motion
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, All the simple harmonic motions are necessarily periodic motions. Simple harmonic motion is defined by a restoring force proportional to the displacement and directed back towards the mean position, and that condition forces the displacement to follow a sine or cosine of time. A sine repeats after a fixed interval, so every simple harmonic motion repeats itself at regular intervals and is periodic. The reverse does not hold: a motion can repeat without the force being proportional to displacement.

question: The radar used by police to check over-speeding vehicles works on the principle of
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Doppler effect. A speed radar sends out a radio wave, the moving vehicle reflects it back, and the returned wave comes home at a slightly different frequency. That shift in frequency caused by relative motion between source and observer is the Doppler effect, and its size is proportional to the vehicle's speed along the line of sight, so measuring the shift measures the speed. The same principle reads the speed of a cricket ball, of blood in an artery and of a distant galaxy.

question: Which one of the following statements with regard to Newton's third law of motion is NOT correct?
opt_a: Force never occurs singly in nature
opt_b: When the earth pulls a stone downwards due to gravity, the stone exerts a force on the earth
opt_c: There is a cause-effect relation implied in the third law
opt_d: There is no cause-effect relation implied in the third law
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, There is a cause-effect relation implied in the third law. The third law says that if a body A exerts a force on a body B, then B exerts an equal and opposite force on A at the same instant. Neither force comes first and neither causes the other; they are two aspects of one interaction. Textbook treatments make the point explicitly, which is why the paired statement (d) is the correct one and (c) is the statement the question asks you to reject.

question: Magnesium is used in
opt_a: fireworks to make a bright white light
opt_c: examination of alimentary canal of the patient
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, fireworks to make a bright white light. Magnesium ignites readily and burns in air with an intense white flame, forming magnesium oxide, and that brilliance is why magnesium powder and ribbon are packed into fireworks, flares and the old photographic flash. The reaction is strongly exothermic and gives out a great deal of light along with the heat.

question: Which one of the following ingredients does NOT constitute paint?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Thiourea (accelerator). An accelerator is a rubber-industry additive: it speeds up vulcanisation, the cross-linking of rubber with sulphur. Paint has no vulcanisation step and so has no use for an accelerator. The other three are genuine paint components: a thinner to adjust flow, an anti-skinning agent to stop a skin forming on stored paint, and a pigment to supply colour and opacity.

question: Which one of the following statements about alkaline earth metals is NOT true?
opt_a: Strontium salts burn with a red flame
opt_b: Barium metal is used in medicine to examine the alimentary canal of a patient by X-ray
opt_c: Green plants need magnesium in order to make the chlorophyll that trap the energy from sunlight in photosynthesis
opt_d: Red colour of gemstone Ruby is due to the element beryllium present in it
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Red colour of gemstone Ruby is due to the element beryllium present in it. Ruby is corundum, crystalline aluminium oxide, and its red comes from a small proportion of chromium replacing aluminium in the lattice. Beryllium has no part in it. Beryllium is the metal of beryl, the mineral family that gives emerald and aquamarine, and even there the green of emerald comes from chromium or vanadium rather than from beryllium itself.

question: Which one of the following gases produces a red light when electricity flows through it?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Neon. Pass an electric discharge through low-pressure neon and it glows a distinctive orange-red. That colour is the reason the gas gave its name to an entire advertising industry, and a tube filled with pure neon needs no coating or filter to produce it. The colour comes from the particular set of energy levels in the neon atom, so each gas in a discharge tube glows in its own characteristic way.

question: Which one of the following methods can be used to remove permanent hardness of water?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Ion-exchange. Permanent hardness is caused by dissolved chlorides and sulphates of calcium and magnesium, which do not decompose on heating. An ion-exchange resin traps those calcium and magnesium ions and releases harmless sodium or hydrogen ions in their place, so the hardness leaves the water with the ions that caused it. This is what a domestic water softener does, and the resin is regenerated with brine once it is loaded.

question: Which one of the following is NOT a component of photochemical smog?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Polyaromatic hydrocarbons. Photochemical smog is the oxidising haze that forms over sunny, traffic-heavy cities when nitrogen oxides and volatile organic compounds react under strong sunlight. Its signature products are ozone, peroxyacetyl nitrate and various aldehydes, with nitric oxide and nitrogen dioxide cycling through as the drivers. Polyaromatic hydrocarbons are a product of incomplete combustion: they come out of coal fires, diesel exhaust and burning tobacco, and are not made by the photochemical reactions themselves.

question: The eukaryotic chromatin is composed of
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, DNA and Protein. Chromatin is the material a eukaryotic chromosome is made of, and it is a complex of DNA wound around histone proteins. About 147 base pairs of DNA coil round each histone octamer to make a nucleosome, nucleosomes string together like beads on a thread, and that thread folds further into the compact chromosome seen at cell division. Take away the protein and there is no chromatin, only naked DNA.

question: In which of the following phylum, would you place an animal with a bilaterally symmetrical, triploblastic body without a true internal cavity (coelom)?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Platyhelminthes. The three features in the stem pick out one phylum between them. Flatworms are the first group in the animal series to show bilateral symmetry together with three germ layers, and they have no body cavity between the gut and the body wall: the space is packed with mesodermal tissue. An animal that is bilateral, triploblastic and acoelomate is a flatworm.

question: During respiration in human beings, the actual place of gaseous exchange is
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Alveoli. The nasal passage, trachea and bronchi are conducting tubes; they warm, moisten and filter the air and carry it in and out, but no gas crosses their walls into the blood. Exchange happens in the alveoli, the tiny air sacs at the ends of the finest bronchioles, where a single layer of flattened cells is separated from a capillary by a barrier under a micrometre thick. Oxygen diffuses across into the blood and carbon dioxide diffuses out.

question: In human body, the hormone which is secreted into blood and which controls the rate of heart beat is
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Adrenaline. Adrenaline is released into the blood by the medulla of the adrenal gland when the body is startled, frightened or under strain, and among its effects is a direct increase in the rate and force of the heartbeat. It also widens the airways, diverts blood to skeletal muscle and raises blood sugar, which together make up the fight-or-flight response.

question: In human beings, certain chemicals which cross the synapse between nerve cells are released from
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, nerve endings of nerve cell. A synapse is the narrow gap between the ending of one neuron and the next cell. When an electrical impulse arrives at the axon terminal, it triggers vesicles stored there to fuse with the membrane and release neurotransmitter molecules into the gap. Those molecules diffuse across and bind receptors on the next cell, starting a fresh impulse. The release happens at the terminal endings, not in the cell body, the nucleus, or along the length of the axon.

question: Which one of the following is the major function of platelets?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Clotting of blood. Platelets, also called thrombocytes, are cell fragments shed from large bone-marrow cells. When a vessel is cut they stick to the damaged wall and to each other, forming a temporary plug, and they release factors that set off the cascade converting fibrinogen into fibrin. The fibrin mesh traps blood cells and hardens the plug into a clot. A shortage of platelets shows up as easy bruising and prolonged bleeding.

question: An electron and a photon have same de Broglie wavelength. It implies that they have the same
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, linear momentum. The de Broglie relation is λ = h/p, and it holds for the electron as a matter wave and for the photon alike, since a photon's momentum is also h/λ. Equal wavelengths therefore force equal momenta, and that is the only quantity the condition fixes. Energy, speed and angular momentum are all free to differ, because the two particles relate energy to momentum by completely different rules.

question: Oil and water do NOT mix because of the property of
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, surface tension. Of the four properties offered, only surface tension describes what happens at the boundary of a liquid. Water molecules attract one another far more strongly than they attract oil molecules, so the boundary between the two carries a high interfacial tension, and the mixture minimises that boundary by pulling the oil together into drops instead of dispersing it. Bulk modulus, shear strain and volume behaviour all describe what a material does through its interior, and none of them says anything about an interface.

question: At triple point the substance co-exists in 1. Liquid phase 2. Solid phase 3. Vapour phase Select the correct answer using the code given below:
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, 1, 2 and 3. The triple point of a substance is the one combination of temperature and pressure at which its solid, liquid and vapour phases sit in equilibrium together. On a phase diagram it is the single point where the fusion, vaporisation and sublimation curves meet, and all three phases are present at once, so every one of the three listed phases belongs in the answer.

question: Latent heat corresponds to the change in heat at constant
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, temperature only. Latent heat is the heat a substance takes in or gives out while changing phase, and the defining feature of that exchange is that the thermometer does not move. Energy going into melting ice at 0 °C is spent breaking the bonds that hold the lattice together rather than raising the kinetic energy of the molecules, so the temperature stays put until the last of the ice is gone. Volume changes sharply during a phase change, which rules out the options that include it.

question: Which one of the following statements on photoelectric effect is NOT correct?
opt_a: Albert Einstein received the Nobel Prize in Physics for explaining photoelectric effect
opt_b: For each metal, there is a threshold frequency ν₀ below which this effect is not observed
opt_c: At a frequency ν > ν₀, the kinetic energy of ejected electrons does not change on increasing the frequency of incident light
opt_d: The number of electrons ejected is proportional to the intensity of incident light
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, At a frequency ν > ν₀, the kinetic energy of ejected electrons does not change on increasing the frequency of incident light. This is the one false statement. Einstein's photoelectric equation gives the maximum kinetic energy as hν minus the work function, so it climbs in a straight line as the frequency of the light is raised. A graph of maximum kinetic energy against frequency is a straight line whose slope is the Planck constant, which is how h was first measured this way.

question: Which one of the following is the average atomic mass of chlorine atom?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, 35.5 u. Chlorine occurs in nature as two stable isotopes, chlorine-35 and chlorine-37, in a ratio close to 3 to 1. The average atomic mass is the weighted mean of the two, so it is (3 × 35 + 1 × 37) divided by 4, which is 142 ÷ 4 = 35.5 u. That is why the periodic table prints a fractional value for chlorine even though no single chlorine atom weighs 35.5 units.

question: Which one of the following is NOT a heterocyclic aromatic compound?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Tropolone. A heterocyclic compound has at least one atom other than carbon inside the ring. Tropolone's ring is a seven-membered carbon ring carrying a hydroxyl and a carbonyl group on the outside, with no heteroatom in the ring itself, so it is carbocyclic: aromatic in the non-benzenoid sense, but not heterocyclic. Furan, thiophene and pyridine each carry a heteroatom in the ring and are the standard textbook examples of aromatic heterocycles.

question: Which one of the following minerals is NOT a naturally occurring silicate?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Bauxite. Bauxite is not a single mineral but a rock made mostly of aluminium hydroxide minerals such as gibbsite, boehmite and diaspore, together with iron oxides and clay. It contains no silicate framework and is the ore from which aluminium is won. Feldspar, zeolite and mica are all built on linked silicon-oxygen tetrahedra and are silicates in the strict sense.

question: In which part of the cell, the glucose is converted into pyruvate?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Cytoplasm. The breakdown of glucose to pyruvate is glycolysis, and its ten enzyme-catalysed steps all take place in the cytoplasm, outside any organelle. Glycolysis needs no oxygen and happens in every living cell, prokaryotic and eukaryotic alike. What happens to the pyruvate afterwards is what varies: in the presence of oxygen it moves into the mitochondrion for complete oxidation, and without oxygen it is converted to lactate or to ethanol.

question: After fertilization, the ovule and ovary subsequently develop to form
opt_d: degenerated ovule and seedless fruit respectively
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, seed and fruit respectively. After fertilisation the ovule, which contains the fertilised egg, matures into the seed, and the ovary that enclosed the ovules ripens into the fruit around them. The correspondence is one of containment: what held the ovules becomes what holds the seeds. Everything else in the flower (petals, sepals, stamens and style) usually withers away.

question: Which one of the following statements is correct?
opt_a: Glucose breaks down to CO₂, H₂O and energy in all organisms
opt_b: Glucose breaks down into ethanol, CO₂ and energy in our muscle cells
opt_c: Glucose breaks down into CO₂, H₂O and energy in all aerobic tissues
opt_d: Glucose breaks down into lactate and energy in yeast
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Glucose breaks down into CO₂, H₂O and energy in all aerobic tissues. Complete oxidation to carbon dioxide and water is what respiration achieves when oxygen is available, and any tissue respiring aerobically ends there. The qualifier 'aerobic' is what makes this statement safe, and the absence of that qualifier is what sinks option (a).

question: Growing two or more crops in the same field but in different rows is called
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Inter cropping. Intercropping means growing two or more crops together on the same field in a definite row pattern: a few rows of one crop alternating with a few rows of another, as with soybean and pigeon pea, or groundnut and sunflower. The defined arrangement is what separates it from mixed cropping, where the seeds are simply sown together without any pattern.

question: Who among the following won the Fed Cup Heart Award, 2020?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Sania Mirza. The Fed Cup is the women's team championship of world tennis, so of the four Indian sportswomen listed only Sania Mirza is eligible to have played in it at all. The award was announced on 11 May 2020 for the Asia and Oceania zone and made her the first Indian ever to win it, after she returned to the Indian team at the tie in Dubai and India reached the play-offs for the first time.

question: National Technology Day is observed on
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, 11 May. National Technology Day marks 11 May 1998, when India carried out the Pokhran-II nuclear tests, flew the indigenous Hansa-3 light aircraft for the first time and successfully test-fired the Trishul surface-to-air missile. Three technological milestones fell on one day, and the government designated it accordingly, with the observance beginning the following year.

question: Which one of the following ships was deployed in ‘Mission Sagar’, which was sent to different countries carrying Food and COVID related items on 10 May 2020?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, INS Kesari. Mission Sagar began on 10 May 2020 when INS Kesari sailed for the Maldives, Mauritius, Seychelles, Madagascar and Comoros with food stores, COVID-related medicines including hydroxychloroquine, Ayurvedic medicines and naval medical assistance teams aboard. Kesari is a landing ship tank, an amphibious vessel with cargo holds and space for troops, which is why it and not a frigate was chosen to carry hundreds of tonnes of relief.

question: Which one of the following has the largest contribution to the Gross Tax Revenue of Government of India in 2019-20 (BE)?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Corporation Tax. In the Budget Estimates for 2019-20 the Centre's gross tax revenue was put at about 24.61 lakh crore rupees, and corporation tax at 7.66 lakh crore rupees was the largest single head within it. Goods and Services Tax came next at about 6.63 lakh crore, taxes on income other than corporation tax at 5.69 lakh crore, union excise duties at 3 lakh crore and customs at about 1.56 lakh crore.

question: What is meant by MSME?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises. That is the statutory expansion, fixed by the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises Development Act, 2006, which created the three categories and the ministry that administers them. Micro, small and medium are successive size bands, so the three words are a graded sequence rather than a mixed list of adjectives.

question: Which one of the following is the top ranking country in the World Economic Forum's 74th Global Energy Transition Index?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Sweden. Sweden headed the World Economic Forum's Energy Transition Index in its 2020 edition, as it had in the two editions before, with Switzerland second and Finland third. India was placed 74th of the 115 countries ranked, which is where the number printed in this stem comes from: it is India's rank, not an edition number, since the index has run only since the middle of the last decade.

question: Operation Sadbhavna is an initiative of
opt_d: Indian Army and UN Peacekeeping Mission
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Indian Army. Operation Sadbhavna is the Indian Army's civic-action and outreach programme, run mainly in Jammu and Kashmir and extended to Ladakh and parts of the North-East. It runs Army Goodwill Schools, medical camps, vocational training centres, women's empowerment projects, infrastructure works and national integration tours for young people from the region, and it is separate from the Army's operational tasks.

question: Which one among the following is the equivalent rank of 'Wing Commander' of Indian Air Force in Indian Army?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Lieutenant Colonel. The three services share a single ladder of equivalent ranks, and Wing Commander in the Air Force sits level with Lieutenant Colonel in the Army and Commander in the Navy. It is the rank immediately above Squadron Leader, which matches an Army Major, and immediately below Group Captain, which matches an Army Colonel.

question: What is the minimum reduction in projected demand of conventional energy at the end of five years as per the 'development of solar cities' programme?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, 10 per cent. Under the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy's Development of Solar Cities programme, a solar city is one that achieves a minimum ten per cent reduction in its projected demand for conventional energy at the end of five years. The reduction is to be reached by combining energy-efficiency measures with a larger supply from renewable sources within the city, and around sixty cities and towns were proposed for support.

question: Which one of the following countries has suggested the name 'Amphan' to the cyclone that devastated parts of West Bengal and Bangladesh in May 2020?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Thailand. Cyclone names for the north Indian Ocean come from a list contributed by the member countries of a regional panel, and the name Amphan was Thailand's contribution. It was in fact the last name remaining on the list drawn up in 2004, which is why the India Meteorological Department released a fresh list of names shortly before this storm formed. Amphan struck the coast of West Bengal and then Bangladesh in May 2020.

question: Natural Population Change is calculated by
opt_a: subtracting the death rate from the birth rate
opt_b: multiplying the death rate with the birth rate
opt_c: adding the death rate with the birth rate
opt_d: subtracting the birth rate from the death rate
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, subtracting the death rate from the birth rate. Natural population change counts only births and deaths, leaving migration out. Subtracting the crude death rate from the crude birth rate gives the rate of natural increase, and where deaths outnumber births the figure turns negative, which is natural decrease. Adding migration to this gives the total change in a population.

question: A long narrow stretch of sand and/or shingle with one end attached to the mainland is called
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Sand spit. A spit is a ridge of sand or shingle built by longshore drift, attached to the land at one end and running out into open water at the other, often with a hooked or curved free end where waves refract round it. The stem's two conditions (long and narrow, and joined to the mainland at one end only) describe exactly that.

question: Which one of the following does NOT illustrate the importance of the Coral Reef?
opt_a: They provide employment to the people
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, They protect communities from earthquakes. A reef is a limestone ridge built on the sea floor by colonial polyps. It sits on the crust, not inside it, so nothing about a coral framework damps the ground shaking that an earthquake sends through rock. Reefs do absorb wave energy , which is why the other three options are all genuine reef benefits — wave energy and seismic energy travel through different media. Even for a tsunami, the one earthquake consequence a reef can blunt, the reef works on the water, not on the quake, and only the wave reaches it.

question: Which one of the following statements about the Acacia tree is/are correct? 1. It has a long shallow root system which enables it to find moisture 2. It has thorny leaves to prevent water loss 3. It has wide crown so the foliage can absorb the maximum Sunlight Select the correct answer using the code given below:
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, 1, 2 and 3. The acacia is the standard textbook tree of hot dry lands, and all three statements describe adaptations it is described by. Its roots run long and near the surface so that a wide area of ground is tapped for the little rain that falls, which the statement calls a long shallow root system. Its leaves are reduced to thorns and small leaflets, cutting the surface from which water can evaporate. Its crown spreads wide and flat, so the small amount of foliage it does carry is spread out to catch sunlight rather than stacked in shade. Together they describe a plant solving two problems at once: hold on to water, and still gather enough light to live.

question: Dardic group of language belongs to which language family?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Indo European. The Dardic languages (Kashmiri, Shina, Khowar, Kalasha, Pashai and their neighbours in the north-western Himalaya and the Hindu Kush) form a group inside the Indo-Aryan branch. Indo-Aryan sits under Indo-Iranian, and Indo-Iranian under Indo-European, so Dardic is Indo-European at the family level. Kashmiri is the member most candidates will already know, because it is the Dardic language listed in the Eighth Schedule of the Constitution.

question: 2011 Census has divided the working population of India into four major categories. Which one of the following is NOT one of them?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Domestic workers. The 2011 Census sorts every worker into exactly four categories: cultivators , agricultural labourers , workers in household industry, and other workers . A cook, a driver or a maid employed in a private home is counted — but inside the residual fourth category of other workers, not under any separate Census head called domestic workers. Options (a), (c) and (d) name three of the four real categories, so the fourth, other workers, is the one the question quietly leaves out and replaces with a plausible substitute.

question: Which of the following statements about employment situation in India according to periodic Labour Force Survey 2017-18 is/are correct ? 1. Construction sector gave employment to nearly one-tenth of urban male workforce in India 2. Nearly one-fourth of urban female workers in India were working in manufacturing sector 3. One-fourth of rural female workers in India were engaged in the agriculture sector Select the correct answer using the code given below:
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, 1 and 2 only. Statement 3 is the one that fails, and it fails by a wide margin rather than a fine one. Rural women who work in India work overwhelmingly on the land — roughly three-quarters of them were in agriculture at the time of the 2017-18 survey — so putting the figure at one-fourth understates it by about three times. The first two statements survive: construction absorbed close to a tenth of urban male workers , the single most striking fact about male work in Indian towns, and manufacturing absorbed close to a quarter of urban women workers, their largest single sector.

question: Kumar used to eat 30 samosas in a month when the price of each samosa was ₹12. When the price of samosa increased to ₹15 per piece, he eats only 20 samosas a month. What is the price elasticity of demand for samosa by Kumar?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, 1·33. Price elasticity of demand is the percentage change in quantity divided by the percentage change in price, as a magnitude. Quantity falls from 30 to 20, a change of 10 on a base of 30, or 33·33 per cent; price rises from ₹12 to ₹15, a change of 3 on a base of 12, or 25 per cent. Dividing gives 33·33 ÷ 25 = 1·33 . A cross-check confirms it: elasticity above 1 means demand is elastic, and elastic demand means a price rise cuts total spending — Kumar's outlay falls from 30 × 12 = ₹360 to 20 × 15 = ₹300, exactly as it should.

question: Which of the following goods are included to estimate food inflation in India? 1. Wheat 2. Paddy 3. Tobacco 4. Sugar Select the correct answer using the code given below:
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, 1, 2 and 4. Wheat , paddy and sugar are all food; tobacco is not, and that single distinction decides the whole item, because every one of the other three options includes tobacco. In the wholesale price index, wheat and paddy sit in the food articles group under primary articles and sugar sits under manufactured food products, and the food index is built from both together. Raw tobacco is classified with the non-food articles, and in the consumer price index it has a group of its own — pan, tobacco and intoxicants — kept apart from food and beverages.

question: In which of the following states high yielding varieties of food grains were introduced as part of the first phase of Green Revolution (1966-72)? 1. Andhra Pradesh 2. Tamil Nadu 3. Punjab 4. Haryana Select the correct answer using the code given below:
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, 3 and 4 only. The first phase of the Green Revolution was a wheat revolution , deliberately concentrated where irrigation was already assured: Punjab , Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh. Dwarf Mexican wheat varieties needed heavy, reliable water and heavy fertiliser to deliver their yield, so they went first to the districts that could supply both. Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu are rice country, and the rice varieties that transformed their deltas arrived in the second phase, during the 1970s and after — not in the 1966 to 1972 window the question specifies.

question: Which of the following is/are the most distinctive artefacts of the Harappan Civilisation? 1. Steatite seal 2. Bricks of a standardised ratio 3. Gold bangles 4. Silver spittoon Select the correct answer using the code given below:
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, 1 and 2 only. Distinctive means diagnostic: an object that lets an archaeologist call a site Harappan rather than something else. The steatite seal, square, small and carved with an animal and a line of the undeciphered script, is the signature artefact of the civilisation and is found nowhere outside its orbit. The baked brick made to a fixed ratio of one to two to four in thickness, width and length is the other, because the same ratio recurs from Sindh to Gujarat to Haryana and implies a shared standard rather than local habit. Gold bangles are not diagnostic; goldwork appears in many ancient cultures and Harappan gold is modest in quantity. A silver spittoon is not a Harappan object at all.

question: Which one of the following is NOT listed as one of the sixteen mahajanapadas in the pre-Mauryan period?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Kalinga. The list of sixteen mahajanapadas comes from Buddhist texts, chiefly the Anguttara Nikaya, and runs Anga, Magadha, Kashi, Kosala, Vajji, Malla, Chedi, Vatsa, Kuru, Panchala, Matsya, Surasena, Assaka, Avanti, Gandhara and Kamboja. Kalinga is absent from it. Kalinga enters the record prominently only later: first as the region Ashoka conquered in the war that changed his policy, and then under Kharavela of the Chedi line, whose Hathigumpha inscription is its great source. Kuru, Vatsa and Gandhara are all on the list of sixteen.

question: Which of the following are prescribed as the duties of Vaishyas according to the Dharmashastras? 1. Studying the Vedas 2. Engaging in trade Select the correct answer using the code given below:
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Both 1 and 2. The Dharmashastras give the Vaishya a set of duties that includes both. Trade is the occupation the varna is named for, along with agriculture and the tending of cattle. Studying the Vedas belongs to it as well, because the Vaishya is one of the three twice-born varnas: entitled to the sacred-thread ceremony and therefore to Vedic study. What the texts reserve to the Brahmana alone is not study but teaching, and with it the performing of sacrifices for others and the receiving of gifts. A Vaishya may study the Veda, commission a sacrifice and make gifts; he may not teach, officiate or receive.

question: Which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. The Satavahanas ruled over parts of western India and the Deccan 2. The Satavahanas repaired and rebuilt Sudarshana Lake Select the correct answer using the code given below:
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, 1 only. The Satavahanas did rule over parts of western India and the Deccan; their core lay in what is now Maharashtra and the Andhra country, with Pratishthana, modern Paithan on the Godavari, as their principal capital. The second statement transfers the credit for Sudarshana Lake to the wrong dynasty. That reservoir in Saurashtra was built under Chandragupta Maurya by his governor Pushyagupta, given conduits under Ashoka, and repaired after a storm burst its embankment by Rudradaman, the Shaka Kshatrapa ruler: an event recorded in his own Junagadh rock inscription of about the middle of the second century CE. It was repaired again under the Guptas. The Satavahanas are nowhere in that sequence.

question: In relation to the fundamental duties enshrined in the Constitution of India, which one of the following is NOT correct?
opt_a: The fundamental duties were not originally a part of the Constitution
opt_b: To safeguard public property and abjure violence are fundamental duties
opt_c: They are not enforceable through writs
opt_d: They may not be used for determining constitutionality of laws
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, They may not be used for determining constitutionality of laws. Fundamental duties cannot be enforced against a citizen, but courts do use them when judging a law. Where a statute is challenged under Article 14 or Article 19 and the court finds that it gives effect to a fundamental duty, that finding weighs in favour of holding the restriction reasonable and saving the law. The Supreme Court has also treated the duties as an aid to interpreting ambiguous provisions, holding them as important as the fundamental rights in shaping the constitutional scheme. So the blanket statement in option (d) is the one that does not hold; the other three are accurate.

question: The Governor of a state may exercise discretionary powers when 1. he or she is not convinced by the advice of the Council of Ministers 2. the Constitution requires him/her to act in his/her discretion in certain matters 3. he or she is appointed as the administrator of an adjoining Union Territory Select the correct answer using the code given below:
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, 1, 2 and 3. Statements 2 and 3 are plain constitutional text: Article 163(1) binds the Governor to ministerial advice except where the Constitution requires him to act in his discretion (statement 2), and Article 239(2) lets him be appointed administrator of an adjoining Union Territory, where he acts independently of his State Council of Ministers (statement 3). Statement 1 is looser in wording, but it is carried by Article 163(2) : if a question arises whether a matter falls within the Governor's discretion, his own decision is final and cannot be called in question. A Governor unpersuaded by his ministers is therefore the judge of whether he must follow them — a position the President does not occupy.

question: Which one of the following is NOT true of socialism?
opt_a: Socialists analyse society in terms of income distribution
opt_b: It emphasises the centrality of community
opt_c: Socialists believe that class divisions in society are a fact and therefore irremediable
opt_d: It believes that material benefits should be distributed on the basis of need
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, It emphasises the centrality of community. The key treats community as the odd idea out among the four. The case for that reading is that socialism's own starting point is class — a society read through who owns the means of production and how its product is shared — and its remedy is common or social ownership. Where a doctrine puts community itself at the centre, as communitarianism and conservative organicism do, the community is the primary unit and everything else follows from it; in socialism, co-operative and communal life is presented as the consequence of ending class division, not the axis of the theory. This is the most argued-over item on the 2020 paper — the competing reading of option (c) is set out below — but the official key marks (b), and the key header records that no item was dropped from this paper.

question: Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below the Lists: List I (Concept) - List II (Explanation/Aim) A. Pluralist democracy - 1. Power is always exercised by a privileged few B. People's democracy - 2. Highest and harmonious development of individual capacities C. Developmental democracy - 3. Social equality through common ownership of wealth D. Elitist democracy - 4. Capacity of groups to ensure Governmental responsiveness Code:
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, A-4, B-3, C-2, D-1. Two of the pairs give themselves away by their own words and settle the code. Elitist democracy is the model that says real power always rests with a privileged few however wide the franchise, so D goes to 1. Developmental democracy is the model, running from Rousseau to John Stuart Mill, that values participation because it develops the capacities of the participants, so C goes to 2. People's democracy is the Marxist-Leninist term, and its aim is social equality through common ownership of wealth, which is 3. Pluralist democracy sees politics as competition between organised groups whose pressure keeps government responsive, which is 4.

question: Which one of the following Central Public Sector Undertakings (CPSUs) is recognized as Miniratnas?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Airport Authority of India. The Airports Authority of India (the paper prints the name without the plural) is a Miniratna Category-I central public sector enterprise under the Ministry of Civil Aviation, managing airports and the country's air navigation services. The other three sit higher on the ladder. Indian Oil Corporation and Steel Authority of India were both in the first group of companies granted Maharatna status, in 2010 and 2011. Hindustan Aeronautics was a Navratna at the time of this examination, so it too stood above the Miniratna tier when the paper was set.

question: Which one of the following educational development indicators is currently used by United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) to construct Human Development Index?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Mean Years of Schooling. Since the Human Development Report of 2010 the education dimension of the index has been measured by two indicators together: mean years of schooling , the average number of years of education already completed by adults aged twenty-five and over, and expected years of schooling , the number a child entering school today can expect to receive. Only one of the two is offered here, and it is mean years of schooling. The other two dimensions are health, measured by life expectancy at birth, and standard of living, measured by gross national income per head at purchasing power parity.

question: Which one of the following was recognized as 'invisible hand' by Adam Smith?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Market/Price Mechanism. Adam Smith used the phrase once in the Wealth of Nations, in 1776, to describe how a trader pursuing only his own gain is led as if by an invisible hand to promote an end that formed no part of his intention. The hand is a metaphor for the price mechanism. Prices carry information about scarcity and about what people want, and buyers and sellers responding to them independently produce a co-ordinated outcome that nobody planned. The whole force of the image is that the co-ordination happens without a director, which is why none of the three institutions offered can be it.

question: Fixation of price levels for wheat and rice by the Commission for Agriculture Costs and Prices (CACP) is an example of?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Support Price. What the Commission for Agricultural Costs and Prices recommends is a minimum support price , a floor announced before the sowing season so that a farmer knows the least he will get if he grows the crop. It supports the producer against a collapse in the market and does not cap what he may earn if the market runs above it. That one-sided character is what makes it a support price rather than any of the other three names on offer.

question: Mobile phone operators market in India is an example of
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Oligopoly. An oligopoly is a market with a small number of sellers, each large enough that its pricing changes what the others do, and protected by high barriers to entry. Indian mobile telephony fits this: a handful of operators serve the whole country, spectrum has to be bought at auction and networks cost enormous sums to build, so entry is closed to all but the very large. The tell-tale sign is interdependence : when one operator cuts tariffs the others follow within weeks, behaviour that neither a monopolist nor a firm in a crowd of small sellers would show.

question: Which of the following sectors contribute in recent years to the deterioration of asset quality of commercial banks by way of Non-Performing Assets ? 1. Agriculture and allied sector 2. Industrial sector 3. Infrastructure sector 4. Information technology sector Select the correct answer using the code given below :
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, 2 and 3 only. The bad-loan problem Indian banks carried through the 2010s came out of industry and infrastructure . Lending to large corporate borrowers in steel, power, telecom, roads, textiles and mining was made in the boom years on demand projections that did not materialise, and when projects were delayed by land, fuel-linkage and clearance problems the borrowers could not service the debt. The Reserve Bank's asset quality review in 2015 forced banks to recognise those exposures honestly, and the stressed accounts that surfaced were overwhelmingly of that kind. Agriculture generates non-performing assets too, but its share is small; information technology funds itself largely from its own cash and is not a stressed sector at all.

question: The distance between two successive crests or troughs of sea waves is called as
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Wavelength. Wavelength is the horizontal distance between two successive points in the same phase of a wave — for a sea wave, crest to crest or trough to trough. The other three options are all real oceanographic quantities, and each measures something different: one a vertical distance, one a rate, and one a length of open water rather than a property of the wave at all.

question: Which one of the following is NOT a Mediterranean country ?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, North Sudan. Five African countries have a Mediterranean coastline, and running west to east they are Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Libya and Egypt. Sudan is not among them. Its coast faces the Red Sea, with Port Sudan as its principal harbour, and the country is separated from the Mediterranean by the whole width of Egypt. The paper's phrasing is worth a note: after South Sudan became independent in 2011 the northern remainder is officially just the Republic of the Sudan, and North Sudan is an informal way of naming it.

question: PAHAL, an initiative to transfer the subsidy to direct bank account of the beneficiaries, is related to
opt_d: Central Government Employees for medical treatment
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, LPG consumers. PAHAL, from Pratyaksh Hanstantrit Labh, is the direct benefit transfer scheme for domestic cooking gas. It was launched in fifty-four districts in November 2014 and taken nationwide from January 2015. Under it the consumer buys the cylinder at the market price and the subsidy is paid straight into a bank account linked to the connection, usually through Aadhaar. That design removes the discount at the till and with it the incentive to divert subsidised cylinders into the commercial market, which was the leakage the scheme was built to close. Its scale earned it recognition in the Guinness World Records as the largest household cash-transfer programme in the world.

question: Which one of the following karst landforms is the largest in size ?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Polje. Karst depressions form a size ladder, and the polje sits at the top of it. A polje is a large flat-floored basin, often several kilometres long and sometimes tens of kilometres, enclosed by steep limestone walls, with a floor of alluvium that can be farmed and a stream that crosses part of it before vanishing into a swallow hole. Below it comes the uvala, formed where neighbouring dolines run together, measured in hundreds of metres. Below that come the individual sinkhole and the swallow hole, each measured in metres or tens of metres.

question: Singapore is known as Port of Call because
opt_a: it deals in the processing and shipping of oil
opt_b: it is a deep water port built away from the actual port
opt_c: it is on main sea route where ships use to anchor for refueling, watering and taking food items
opt_d: it serves the parent ports by receiving the ships which are unable to approach due to their large size
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, it is on main sea route where ships use to anchor for refueling, watering and taking food items. That is what a port of call is: a halt on a long voyage where a vessel takes on fuel, fresh water and provisions and may make small repairs, rather than a destination where cargo is loaded or discharged. Singapore sits at the southern end of the Strait of Malacca , on the shortest route between the Indian Ocean and the Pacific, so almost everything moving between the two passes its door. It is today the world's largest bunkering port, which is the modern form of exactly the function the option describes.

question: Which one of the following statements with regard to Censure Motion is NOT correct?
opt_a: A leave of the House is required to move it
opt_b: The Government is free to fix time and date for its discussion
opt_c: It can also be moved against the entirety of the Council of Ministers
opt_d: The Speaker decides whether the motion is in order
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, A leave of the House is required to move it. Leave of the House is the requirement attached to a motion of no confidence , where the Speaker asks whether leave is granted and at least fifty members must rise in support before the motion can be admitted. A censure motion carries no such threshold. It is moved like any other substantive motion, the Speaker rules on whether it is in order, and if admitted the government decides when time will be found for it. The other three statements describe the censure motion accurately.

question: Which one of the following is NOT a correct feature of a Money Bill?
opt_a: It can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha
opt_b: A Deputy Speaker can also certify a Money Bill in case of office of Speaker falling vacant
opt_c: A Speaker's authority is final as to whether a bill is Money Bill or not
opt_d: It can be referred to a joint committee of the two Houses
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, It can be referred to a joint committee of the two Houses. The whole design of the Money Bill procedure keeps the Rajya Sabha out of any decision-making role, so no joint-deliberation mechanism applies. The Council of States must return the bill within fourteen days with or without recommendations, which the Lok Sabha may accept or reject as it pleases; the bill is deemed passed by both Houses regardless. Article 108 , which provides for a joint sitting to resolve a deadlock, expressly does not apply to a Money Bill, because on a Money Bill a deadlock cannot arise. The other three statements are accurate.

question: The idea of social justice requires that 1. equal treatment be supplemented with principle of proportionality 2. due and equal consideration is given to all individuals 3. equality of treatment be transcended to recognise special needs Select the correct answer using the code given below:
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, 2 and 3 only. The two statements the key keeps are the two limbs of social justice in Indian constitutional argument. Due and equal consideration for every individual is the bedrock — the same rules, the same standing and the same weight given to each person's claim, which is the content of equality before the law and of equal opportunity. Going beyond equal treatment to recognise special needs is the second limb: it justifies reservation, special provision for scheduled castes and tribes, and the directive in Article 46 to promote the weaker sections' interests. Statement 1's proportionality, rewarding people differently by effort or skill, belongs to distributive justice and explains unequal reward — not what social justice here means.

question: Which one of the following statements about the Attorney-General of India is NOT correct?
opt_a: The person must be qualified to be appointed as a judge of the Supreme Court
opt_b: He/she enjoys right of audience only in the Supreme Court and High Courts in India
opt_c: He/she holds office during the pleasure of the President
opt_d: He/she receives remuneration as determined by the President
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, He/she enjoys right of audience only in the Supreme Court and High Courts in India. Article 76(3) is explicit that the Attorney-General has the right of audience in all courts in the territory of India, and the word all is the point of the provision. No other advocate holds that right by virtue of office; it exists so that the first law officer can appear for the Union anywhere it is a party, from a district court upwards. The word only in option (b) contradicts the article, and the other three statements reproduce Article 76 accurately.

question: Which of the following is/are correct in relation to the Panchayats? 1. Only the Parliament may endow Panchayats with powers and authority 2. A state may devolve powers to Panchayats in preparation of plans for economic development and social justice 3. A state may devolve powers to Panchayats in implementation of schemes for economic development and social justice Select the correct answer using the code given below:
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, 2 and 3. Article 243G says that the Legislature of a State may, by law, endow the Panchayats with such powers and authority as may be necessary to enable them to function as institutions of self-government, including the preparation of plans for economic development and social justice and the implementation of schemes for economic development and social justice. Statements 2 and 3 are the two limbs of that provision, quoted almost word for word. Statement 1 gets the authority wrong: the power to endow belongs to the State Legislature, not to Parliament, and that division is deliberate, because local government is a State subject and the Seventy-third Amendment created a framework rather than a transfer.

question: Which one of the following statements about the Bhakti Movement in South India is NOT correct?
opt_a: The Nalayira Divyaprabandham was also known as the Tamil Veda
opt_c: Karaikkal Ammaiyar was a devotee of Vishnu
opt_d: Metal images of the saints Appar and Sundarar were made and then consecrated in a Shiva temple
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Karaikkal Ammaiyar was a devotee of Vishnu. Karaikkal Ammaiyar was a devotee of Shiva and one of the sixty-three Nayanars: one of only three women among them. Her story is the one about renouncing beauty; having been recognised as a goddess by her husband, she asked Shiva to take away her form and give her the gaunt shape of a ghoul so that she could sit at his feet. Everything about her belongs to the Shaiva stream, and the option moves her into the Vaishnava one. The other three statements are accurate as they stand.

question: Who among the following is the author of the Kiratarjuniya?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Bharavi. The Kiratarjuniya is Bharavi's, composed in about the sixth century, and it is one of the five great Sanskrit court epics. Its subject comes from the Vana Parva of the Mahabharata: Arjuna's austerities in the Himalaya and his combat with Shiva, who has come disguised as a kirata, a mountain hunter, before granting him the Pashupata weapon. Sanskrit criticism remembers Bharavi for weight of meaning, which is why the traditional verse of praise gives him arthagaurava while giving Magha the gift of simile and Kalidasa that of expression.

question: Which one of the following is the correct description of Kandaria Mahadeo?
opt_b: The title of a work by Bhatti
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, A temple at Khajuraho. The Kandariya Mahadeva is the largest and the most elaborate of the Khajuraho temples, built in about the eleventh century under the Chandella ruler Vidyadhara. It is a Shiva temple in the Nagara style, raised on a high platform, with a shikhara that gathers dozens of subsidiary spires rising towards a single peak in imitation of a mountain range. The other three options are each a true fact fastened to the wrong name, which is what makes the item worth reading carefully.

question: Consider the following statements about the Lingayats: 1. They bury their dead 2. They are great believers in the caste system, especially in the theory of purity and pollution 3. They are against child marriage and favour widow remarriage Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, 1 and 3. The Lingayats bury their dead rather than cremating them, which follows from their belief about death: the devotee unites with Shiva and does not return, so the rites built around rebirth have no place. That is statement 1. They also set themselves against practices the Dharmashastras approved, opposing child marriage and supporting the remarriage of widows , which is statement 3. Statement 2 inverts the movement's most famous position: far from believing in caste and in purity and pollution, the Virashaivas rejected caste distinction and the ritual authority resting on it, and their vachana poets said so in plain Kannada. Note how the codes are printed: option (a) is 1 and 2 and option (b) is 1 only, not the order a candidate expects — read the letters rather than assuming the usual sequence.

question: At which one of the following places is the Vitthala temple located?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Hampi. The Vitthala temple stands at Hampi in Karnataka, on the Tungabhadra, in what was the capital of the Vijayanagara empire. It is the most elaborate building on the site, begun in the fifteenth century and extended under Krishnadeva Raya and Achyuta Raya. It is famous for two things: the stone chariot in its courtyard, a shrine to Garuda carved to look like a temple car, and the slender pillars of its great hall, which give out musical notes when struck. Vitthala is a form of Vishnu chiefly worshipped at Pandharpur in Maharashtra, and the Vijayanagara rulers brought the cult south into their capital.

question: In relation to the powers of the Union Government of India, which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
opt_a: The Government of India may undertake legislative functions of a territory outside of India by agreement with the Government of that territory
opt_b: The Union Government may not entrust a State Government with functions over matters where executive power of the Union extends
opt_c: The Union Government may direct States for construction and maintenance of means of communication of military importance
opt_d: The Governor may, with consent of Government of India, entrust its officers with functions on matters which fall within the executive power of the State
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, The Union Government may not entrust a State Government with functions over matters where executive power of the Union extends. Read the words may not carefully — the whole item turns on them, and they are not capitalised or emphasised in any way. Article 258(1) provides the opposite: the President may, with a State's consent, entrust to that Government or its officers functions relating to any matter to which the executive power of the Union extends. This is routine, since the Union has no field machinery of its own in most subjects and works through State officers. The option denies a power the Constitution expressly grants, so it is the one that is not correct.

question: As per provisions of the Constitution of India, which one of the following is correct?
opt_a: Only Parliament has the power to legislate over a subject under the Concurrent List
opt_b: Both Parliament and State Legislatures have the power to legislate over a subject under the Concurrent List
opt_c: A legislation made under the Concurrent List by Parliament should be ratified by half of the State Legislatures so as to become a law of the country
opt_d: Only State Legislatures are empowered to make laws under Concurrent List
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Both Parliament and State Legislatures have the power to legislate over a subject under the Concurrent List. That is the definition of the list. Article 246(2) gives Parliament power over Concurrent List matters and Article 246(3) leaves the States with power over the same list, subject to the Union's. Where both have legislated and the two laws conflict, Article 254 resolves it: the Union law prevails and the State law is void to the extent of the repugnancy, unless the State law was reserved for the President's consideration and received his assent, in which case it prevails within that State, and Parliament may still override it afterwards.

question: Which of the following statement(s) regarding passing a law under the State List is/are correct? 1. Even in the sphere (State List) exclusively reserved for the States, Parliament can legislate under certain circumstances 2. Parliament cannot legislate a subject under the State List under any circumstances 3. A resolution supported by two-thirds of the members present and voting is required to be passed by Rajya Sabha to pass a law under the State List Select the correct answer using the code given below:
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, 1 and 3 only. Statements 1 and 2 contradict each other outright (one says Parliament can legislate on a State List subject in certain circumstances and the other says it cannot under any circumstances) so exactly one of them can be in the answer, which removes option (a) before any knowledge is applied. The true one is statement 1. Parliament reaches the State List through five doors: a Rajya Sabha resolution in the national interest under Article 249, a proclamation of Emergency under Article 250, a request from two or more States under Article 252, the implementation of an international agreement under Article 253, and President's rule under Article 356. Statement 3 states the Article 249 threshold accurately: a resolution of the Council of States supported by not less than two-thirds of the members present and voting.

question: Which of the following statement(s) regarding promulgation of ordinance is/are correct? 1. President can promulgate ordinances which are of temporary duration 2. An ordinance promulgated by the President has to be ratified by Parliament within six weeks of its re-assembly Select the correct answer using the code given below:
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Both 1 and 2. An ordinance under Article 123 is temporary by design. The President may promulgate one only when both Houses of Parliament are not in session and only when he is satisfied that circumstances make immediate action necessary, and it has the same force and effect as an Act of Parliament while it lasts. Its life is short. Under Article 123(2), an ordinance ceases to operate at the expiry of six weeks from the reassembly of Parliament unless it has been approved before then, and it goes earlier still if both Houses pass resolutions disapproving it. So both statements hold. Where the two Houses reassemble on different dates, the six weeks is counted from the later of the two.

question: Match List I with List II and select the correct answer using the code given below the Lists: List I (Name of Shifting Cultivation) A. Milpa B. Ladang C. Rocca D. Masole List II (Country) 1. Zaire 2. Brazil 3. Malaysia 4. Mexico Code:
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, A-4 B-3 C-2 D-1. Two of the four pairs settle the code on their own. Milpa is a Nahuatl word from Mexico and Central America, so A goes to 4. Ladang is Malay and Indonesian, so B goes to 3. Once those are fixed, only one option remains, and it puts Roca with Brazil, which is right (roça is Portuguese and Brazil is the Portuguese-speaking country on the list) and Masole with Zaire in the Congo basin. The paper's spellings and place-names are of their time: Rocca is usually written roça, and the country it calls Zaire has been the Democratic Republic of the Congo since 1997.

question: SAUBHAGYA, a Central Government scheme, is related to
opt_a: providing cash money to women giving birth of single female child
opt_b: connecting kitchen of every household with piped cooking gas
opt_c: strengthening and augmenting infrastructure for piped water supply
opt_d: achieving universal household electrification in the country
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, achieving universal household electrification in the country. SAUBHAGYA is the acronym of the Pradhan Mantri Sahaj Bijli Har Ghar Yojana, announced in September 2017 by the Ministry of Power. Its single job was the last mile: giving an electricity connection to every willing un-electrified household, rural and urban. Village electrification had already been declared complete under the earlier Deendayal Upadhyaya Gram Jyoti Yojana, but a village counted as electrified once its public places and a tenth of its homes were connected, which left crores of individual houses dark. Households on the Socio-Economic and Caste Census 2011 list got the connection free; everyone else paid Rs 500, recovered in ten instalments through the electricity bill. The outlay was Rs 16,320 crore. As of the 2020 exam the scheme was running; it was closed in March 2022 after about 2.82 crore households had been connected.

question: The Cartagena Protocol, to which India is a party, is related to
opt_a: combat the green house gasses and to reduce the global warming and climate change
opt_b: biosafety, negotiated under the aegis of the Convention on Biological Diversity
opt_c: combat the ozone depleting substances to protect the human lives from diseases
opt_d: combat the phenomenon of desertification by improving dry land farming in dry regions
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, biosafety, negotiated under the aegis of the Convention on Biological Diversity. The Cartagena Protocol on Biosafety is the first supplementary agreement to the Convention on Biological Diversity. It was adopted at Montreal on 29 January 2000 and entered into force on 11 September 2003; the name comes from Cartagena in Colombia, where the negotiating session was originally to have concluded in February 1999. What it governs is the transboundary movement of living modified organisms (organisms carrying novel combinations of genetic material) and it works through advance informed agreement, under which an exporter must notify and obtain consent from the importing country before the first shipment of an LMO meant for release into the environment. India ratified it in January 2003, and the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change is the national focal point.

question: Transition zone of varied natural vegetation occupying the boundary between two adjacent and differing plant communities is known as
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, ecotone. An ecotone is the transition belt where two adjacent communities meet and blend, so it carries species from both sides plus species that live nowhere else. Because the conditions change steeply across it, the number of species and often the population density are higher in the ecotone than in either community it separates: the edge effect, and the species restricted to that band are called edge species. Mangroves between land and sea, an estuary between a river and the ocean, and the grassland strip between forest and prairie are the standard examples. The definition in the stem is the definition of an ecotone almost word for word: a transition zone at the boundary between two adjacent and differing plant communities.

question: Consider the following statements about sulh-i kul: 1. It means 'absolute peace' 2. It provided for freedom of expression to all religions and schools of thought 3. The ideal of sulh-i kul was implemented through state policies Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, 1, 2 and 3. All three statements come from the standard account of Abu'l Fazl's writing on Akbar's ideal of governance. Statement 1 is right because sulh-i kul translates as absolute peace, and Abu'l Fazl presents it as the cornerstone of enlightened rule. Statement 2 is right because under sulh-i kul all religions and schools of thought were given freedom of expression, on the single condition that they did not undermine the authority of the state or fight one another. Statement 3 is right because the ideal was not left as court rhetoric: it was carried into policy: the nobility was recruited across Iranis, Turanis, Afghans, Rajputs and Deccanis, the pilgrimage tax went in 1563 and the jizya on non-Muslim subjects in 1564, and grants were made to shrines of several faiths. Since no statement fails, the answer is the option that accepts all three.

question: Which one of the following statements about the religious policies of the Mughal kings is NOT correct?
opt_a: The tax on pilgrimage was abolished in 1563, and the jizya tax on non-Muslim Subjects was abolished in 1564
opt_b: Akbar issues instructions to his officers to follow the policy of religious toleration
opt_c: Not all Mughal emperors gave grants for the building and maintenance of places of worship
opt_d: Grants were issued for the repair of a number of temples in the reigns of Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb, after they had been destroyed during war
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Not all Mughal emperors gave grants for the building and maintenance of places of worship. The item asks for the statement that is NOT correct, and this is it, because the textbook position is the opposite: all the Mughal emperors gave grants to support the building and maintenance of places of worship. Options (a), (b) and (d) each restate a settled fact: Akbar removed the pilgrimage tax in 1563 and the jizya in 1564; he issued instructions to his officers to follow a policy of religious toleration; and grants were issued for the repair of temples in the reigns of Shah Jahan and Aurangzeb after those temples had been destroyed during war. Option (c) inverts that record and is therefore the answer.

question: Tulsidas was the author of 1. Ramcharitmanas 2. Padavali 3. Kavitavali Select the correct answer using the code given below:
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, 1 and 3 only. Tulsidas wrote the Ramcharitmanas and the Kavitavali, but not the Padavali. The Ramcharitmanas is his retelling of the Rama story in Awadhi, begun at Ayodhya in 1574, and it is the work that carried the Rama devotion of the north into everyday recitation. The Kavitavali is also his and also on the Rama story, composed in Braj Bhasha in the kavitta and savaiya metres rather than the chaupai-doha of the Manas. Padavali is not his. The word simply means a collection of padas, and the famous ones belong to other poets: Vidyapati's Maithili Padavali above all, and the collections associated with Chandidas. Since statement 2 fails and the other two hold, the code that takes 1 and 3 is the answer.

question: On which one of the following conditions, did the Marathas agree to serve the Mughal king with a cavalry contingent of 15,000 in the early 18th century?
opt_a: Grant of the jagir of Malwa province
opt_b: Control of the resources of Gujarat
opt_c: The right to levy chauth and sardeshmukhi in the Deccan and South India
opt_d: The right to mint coins in their own name
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, The right to levy chauth and sardeshmukhi in the Deccan and South India. The agreement in question is the settlement of 1719 between Shahu's minister Balaji Vishwanath and the Sayyid brothers, then the effective power at Delhi. Its terms were plain: the Marathas were confirmed in the swarajya, the home territory of Shivaji's kingdom, and were granted the right to collect chauth and sardeshmukhi from the six Mughal provinces of the Deccan; in return they undertook to keep 15,000 horse in the emperor's service, to maintain order in the Deccan and to pay an annual tribute. Chauth was a levy of one-fourth of the assessed revenue; sardeshmukhi was a further one-tenth, claimed on the ground that the Maratha ruler was the hereditary sardeshmukh, or head headman, of the country. The two together turned Maratha raiding into a legal right recognised by the empire.

question: According to the Delimitation Commission of India and subject to Article 333 of the Constitution of India, what is the maximum number of members that a State Legislative Assembly may have?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, 500. Article 170(1) of the Constitution fixes the size of a State Legislative Assembly at not more than five hundred and not less than sixty members, chosen by direct election from territorial constituencies. Five hundred is therefore the ceiling for every State, and no Assembly has come near it: Uttar Pradesh, the largest, has 403 seats. The floor of sixty is relaxed for several small States by special provision, which is why Sikkim has 32, and Goa, Mizoram and the Union Territory of Puducherry sit in the forties and thirties. Delimitation redraws constituency boundaries within a State on the basis of census figures, but it works inside this constitutional ceiling and cannot raise it.

question: Who among the following was the first non-official member to be elected as Speaker of the Central Legislative Assembly on 24-8-1925?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Vithalbhai J Patel. The Central Legislative Assembly created by the Government of India Act, 1919 had been presided over since 1921 by a President nominated by the Governor-General, Sir Frederick Whyte. From 1925 the House elected its own presiding officer, and on 24 August 1925 it chose Vithalbhai Patel, a Swarajist and the elder brother of Vallabhbhai Patel by two years. He was the first elected President of the Assembly and the first Indian to hold the chair. He had entered the Assembly in 1924 as a co-founder of the Swaraj Party alongside C. R. Das and Motilal Nehru, which had gone into the legislatures to obstruct from within after Gandhi suspended non-cooperation in 1922. He resigned the chair in 1930 in support of the Civil Disobedience Movement and died in 1933.

question: Which of the following statements are correct with regard to Speaker/Deputy Speaker, Lok Sabha? 1. On dissolution of the Lok Sabha, both the Speaker and Deputy Speaker cease to be members of the House. 2. Both Speaker and Deputy Speaker vacate their office on dissolution of the Lok Sabha 3. Only Deputy Speaker vacates his office and Speaker shall not vacate his office until immediately before the first meeting of the Lok Sabha after dissolution Select the correct answer using the code given below:
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, 1 and 3 only. Statement 1 is right: dissolution ends the House, so every member ceases to be a member, and the Speaker and Deputy Speaker are members first of all. Statement 3 is right and states the exception written into Article 94: the proviso says the Speaker shall not vacate his office until immediately before the first meeting of the House of the People after the dissolution. There is no such saving for the Deputy Speaker, whose office therefore falls with the House. Statement 2 says both vacate office on dissolution and is wrong for exactly that reason. Notice that statements 2 and 3 contradict one another, so at most one of them can be accepted, which kills option (b) before any recall is needed.

question: With regard to Panel of Chairperson, Lok Sabha, which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. Panel of Chairperson is drawn from the ruling party only 2. Panel of Chairperson is nominated by different political parties and appointed by Speaker, Lok Sabha 3. Panel of Chairperson consists of 10 members and one of them presides over the House when both Speaker and Deputy Speaker are not there Select the correct answer using the code given below:
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, 2 and 3. Statement 1 fails at once: the panel is not drawn from the ruling party alone. It is nominated from among the members of the House by the Speaker, and the practice is to include members from different parties, which is what statement 2 records: a panel put together across the parties and given effect by the Speaker's nomination. Statement 3 gives the panel's size as ten and describes its function correctly: a member of the panel presides only when both the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker are absent, and only then. He has the same powers as the Speaker while in the Chair, but he cannot exercise them once either of the two returns. Taking statements 2 and 3 and rejecting 1 gives option (b).

question: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
opt_a: Mahogany is a timber species of Tropical Rainforest
opt_b: Chaparral vegetation is found in Taiga climate
opt_c: Lichens are predominantly found in Tundra region
opt_d: Sal is a representative species of Moist Deciduous Forest
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Chaparral vegetation is found in Taiga climate. Chaparral belongs to the Mediterranean climate, not the taiga. It is the dense, drought-hardy scrub of California (leathery evergreen leaves, deep roots, plants adapted to burn and regrow) and its counterparts elsewhere carry local names: maquis and garrigue around the Mediterranean Sea, matorral in central Chile, fynbos at the Cape, mallee in southern Australia. Every one of these lies on a west coast between roughly thirty and forty-five degrees of latitude, with rain in winter and drought in summer. The taiga is the opposite kind of place: the subarctic coniferous belt of spruce, fir, pine and larch running across Siberia, Scandinavia and Canada, with long freezing winters and a short cool summer. The three other statements are all correct, which leaves (b) as the answer to a NOT-correct item.

question: Consider the following statements: 1. River Kaveri has well developed valley 2. Valley of River Alakananda is still growing 3. River Krishna is largest east flowing peninsular river Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, 1 and 2. Statement 1 holds: the Kaveri drains the ancient, stable Deccan block, has long been graded, and flows through a broad, mature valley with a wide flood plain and a large delta at its mouth. Statement 2 holds for the opposite reason: the Alakananda is a Himalayan headstream of the Ganga, rising at the Satopanth and Bhagirath Kharak glaciers and joining the Bhagirathi at Devprayag, and it flows through mountains that are still rising, so it is still cutting down and eating headward: its valley is a young, deep gorge that is actively growing. Statement 3 fails on a single fact: the largest east-flowing peninsular river is the Godavari, not the Krishna. The Godavari runs about 1,465 kilometres and drains roughly 3.1 lakh square kilometres, which is why it is called the Dakshin Ganga; the Krishna is the second largest of the group.

question: According to Koppen’s climatic classifications of India, Great Northern Plains are represented by
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Cwg Climate. In the Koppen scheme as applied to India, Cwg is read letter by letter: C is the warm temperate or mesothermal group, in which the coldest month averages between minus three and eighteen degrees Celsius; w means the dry season falls in winter; and g is Koppen's own sub-symbol for the Gangetic type, where the hottest month comes before the summer solstice and the rains. That combination (a hot, dry season ending in June, a wet south-west monsoon, and a cool dry winter) is exactly the Great Northern Plains. The NCERT table on India's climatic regions assigns Cwg to the Ganga plain, eastern Rajasthan, northern Madhya Pradesh and most of the North-East.
