Present-day Koppen maps built from station data give the same plain the label Cwa, since the modern scheme uses 'a' for a hot summer and no longer carries the 'g' sub-symbol; the classification of the region has not changed, only the notation.

question: Which one among the following stations receives maximum rainfall?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, Raipur. Raipur's annual rainfall normal is about 1,290 millimetres, the highest of the four by a clear margin. Bengaluru follows at about 1,078 millimetres, Hyderabad at about 860, and Delhi at about 774. The geography behind the ranking is straightforward: Raipur sits in the Chhattisgarh plain in the upper Mahanadi basin, squarely on the path of the Bay of Bengal branch of the south-west monsoon as it swings up the valley, and it takes almost all that rain between mid-June and early October. Hyderabad lies further inland on the Deccan, on the drier side of the same branch. Bengaluru sits on the Mysore plateau in the rain shadow of the Western Ghats and makes up its total from both monsoons plus heavy pre-monsoon thunderstorms. Delhi is at the far north-western tail of the monsoon, where the current is weakest by the time it arrives.

question: Which one among the following countries does NOT have common boundary with South Africa?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, Zambia. South Africa has six land neighbours and Zambia is not among them. Going round the border: Namibia in the north-west along about 967 kilometres, Botswana across the north along 1,840 kilometres, Zimbabwe on a short northern stretch of 225 kilometres, Mozambique on the north-east along 491 kilometres, Eswatini along 430 kilometres, and Lesotho along 909 kilometres: Lesotho being entirely enclosed by South African territory. The total is about 4,862 kilometres. Zambia's nearest approach is the Kazungula area on the Zambezi, where Zambia, Zimbabwe, Botswana and Namibia come within a few hundred metres of one another; even there Zimbabwe and Botswana lie between Zambia and South Africa.

question: Consider the following statements about the Treaty of Amritsar (1809): 1. The Treaty fixed the Sutlej as the boundary between the Punjab and British India 2. It was after this treaty that Maharaja Ranjit Singh was able to annex Jammu, Multan and Kashmir to his domains Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Both 1 and 2. The Treaty of Amritsar was signed on 25 April 1809 between Ranjit Singh and Charles Metcalfe, sent by Lord Minto. Statement 1 is right: Ranjit Singh gave up his claims over the Sikh chiefships east of the Sutlej, which passed under British protection, and the river became the recognised line between his Punjab and the Company's territory. Statement 2 is right as a consequence of the first: shut out of the cis-Sutlej country, Ranjit Singh turned his army north and west instead. Multan fell in 1818, Kashmir in 1819, and Peshawar was taken in 1834, while Jammu was granted to Gulab Singh in the early 1820s. Neither statement fails, so the answer accepts both.

question: Which one of the following statements about the Harappan script is NOT correct?
opt_a: It has about four hundred signs
opt_b: It was written from right to left
opt_c: It has been found on bone rods and jewellery
opt_d: It refers to the people of Meluhha
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, It refers to the people of Meluhha. Meluhha is not something the Harappan script says; it is what Mesopotamian scribes called a distant land they traded with, and it appears in their cuneiform records, not in the Indus signs. Since the Harappan script has never been deciphered, no claim about what it refers to can be made at all, which is precisely why this statement is the one that fails. The other three are the standard descriptive facts about the script: it runs to roughly four hundred signs, it was generally written from right to left, and it is found on a wide range of objects including bone rods and jewellery as well as seals, copper tools, terracotta tablets and the large signboard from Dholavira.

question: Which of the following statements is/are correct? 1. Parmahansa Mandali was founded in Bengal by Swami Vivekananda 2. Prarthana Samaj was started in Maharashtra with the aim of reforming Hindu religious thought and practice Select the correct answer using the code given below:
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, 2 only. Statement 2 is right: the Prarthana Samaj was founded in Bombay on 31 March 1867 by Atmaram Pandurang, with Waman Abaji Modak, and its declared purpose was the reform of Hindu religious thought and practice: it worked against caste restrictions, child marriage and the ban on widow remarriage, and for women's education. M. G. Ranade joined afterwards and made it the leading reform body of western India. Statement 1 fails on every element it asserts. The Paramahansa Mandali was founded in 1849 in Bombay, that is in Maharashtra and not Bengal, and its moving figure was Dadoba Pandurang, not Swami Vivekananda. Vivekananda belongs to a later generation altogether: he founded the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897.

question: Which one of the following is NOT correct about Mahatma Gandhi's Dandi Yatra or Salt March?
opt_a: It was the first national activity in which women participated in large numbers
opt_b: Gandhiji allowed the women's participation at the request of Kamaladevi Chattopadhyay
opt_c: The march was fully covered by the Western press
opt_d: The march began after the failure of the First Round Table Conference in London
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, The march began after the failure of the First Round Table Conference in London. The chronology is the wrong way round. The Salt March began at Sabarmati on 12 March 1930 and reached Dandi on 6 April, when Gandhi picked up a lump of natural salt and broke the salt law. The First Round Table Conference opened in London only on 12 November 1930, eight months later, and ran to 19 January 1931; the Congress boycotted it entirely, which is why it produced nothing and why Gandhi attended the second session in 1931 after the Gandhi-Irwin Pact. A march cannot have begun after the failure of a conference that had not yet met. The other three statements are all accurate, so option (d) is the answer to a NOT-correct item.

question: The British Committee of the Indian National Congress was founded in
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, 1889. The British Committee of the Indian National Congress was set up in London in 1889 to carry the Congress case to the British public and Parliament, on the Moderate reasoning that British opinion was ignorant of Indian conditions rather than hostile to them. The committee's weekly journal, India, began publication the following year and ran for decades as the movement's voice in Britain. Sir William Wedderburn, a retired civil servant who had twice presided over the Congress, chaired it, and Dadabhai Naoroji worked through it: he went on to win the Central Finsbury seat in the House of Commons in 1892, the first Indian to sit there. The Congress spent a substantial share of its funds on this British work, which is one reason the Extremists later attacked the whole strategy as petitioning.

question: Tamilakam was the name of the ancient Tamil country that included
opt_a: present-day Tamil Nadu as well as parts of Sri Lanka
opt_b: land between present day Tirupati hills and the southernmost tip of peninsula
opt_d: present day Kerala, Telangana and Karnataka
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, land between present day Tirupati hills and the southernmost tip of peninsula. The classical definition comes from the preface to the Tolkappiyam, which places the land where Tamil is spoken as the mother tongue between the northern Venkata hill and the southern Kumari, that is, between the Venkata or Tirupati hills in the north and Kanyakumari at the tip of the peninsula. The Silappadikaram says the same thing in other words, describing the Tamil region as running from the hills of Vishnu in the north to the ocean at the cape in the south. On the modern map this covers Tamil Nadu, Kerala and Puducherry along with the southern edges of Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka. Three dynasties shared it in the Sangam age: the Cheras in the west, the Cholas in the Kaveri valley and the Pandyas around the Vaigai.

question: A member giving notice of a resolution for removal of Speaker, Lok Sabha should be addressed to the
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Secretary General, Lok Sabha. Removing the Speaker is entirely an affair of the House. Article 94 provides that the Speaker may be removed by a resolution of the House of the People passed by a majority of all the then members, and that no such resolution may be moved unless at least fourteen days' notice has been given of the intention to move it. That notice is a communication to the House, and every communication to the House is addressed to the Secretary-General, who heads the Lok Sabha Secretariat and is the officer through whom notices of motions, resolutions and questions are received and circulated. The President, the Prime Minister and the Deputy Speaker have no part in receiving it.

question: Which one of the following statements regarding Public Accounts Committee is correct?
opt_a: It consists of fifteen members from Lok Sabha and seven members from Rajya Sabha
opt_b: It consists of twenty members from Lok Sabha and ten members from Rajya Sabha
opt_c: The term of members of Public Accounts Committee is five years
opt_d: Finance Minister is the Chairperson of the Public Accounts Committee
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, It consists of fifteen members from Lok Sabha and seven members from Rajya Sabha. The Public Accounts Committee has twenty-two members in all: fifteen elected by the Lok Sabha from among its own members and not more than seven by the Rajya Sabha. Election is annual, by the principle of proportional representation through the single transferable vote, so the composition of the Committee mirrors the strength of the parties in each House. The term is one year, not five. The Chairperson is appointed by the Speaker from among the Committee's Lok Sabha members, and by a convention followed since 1967 the Speaker names a member of the Opposition. No Minister may be a member, which disposes of the option that makes the Finance Minister its Chairperson.

question: Which of the following statements with regard to the Speaker, Lok Sabha is/are correct? 1. The election of the Speaker of Lok Sabha is conducted by the Election Commission of India 2. The Speaker on assuming his office is not required to make and subscribe oath or affirmation 3. The Speaker does not exercise a casting vote in case of equality of votes Select the correct answer using the code given below:
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, 2 only. Statement 2 holds: the Speaker takes no separate oath on assuming the chair. Article 99 requires every member of either House to make and subscribe an oath or affirmation before taking his seat, and the Speaker has already done that as a member; no further oath attaches to the office, unlike the President, the Vice-President, judges and Ministers, all of whom are sworn in under specific articles. Statement 1 fails: the Speaker is elected by the members of the Lok Sabha from among themselves, on a date fixed by the President, and the Election Commission has no role: the pro tem Speaker presides over that election. Statement 3 fails too: Article 100(1) gives the person presiding no vote in the first instance but a casting vote in the case of an equality of votes, so the Speaker does exercise a casting vote.

question: Who was the President of the Constituent Assembly?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, Rajendra Prasad. The Constituent Assembly met for the first time on 9 December 1946 with Sachchidananda Sinha, its oldest member, in the chair as provisional President. Two days later, on 11 December 1946, the Assembly elected Rajendra Prasad its permanent President, and he presided over the whole of the constitution-making that followed, signing the Constitution as adopted on 26 November 1949. He went on to become the first President of the Republic in January 1950. The three other names in the option list were all central to the Assembly's work but none of them held its chair.

question: In an exam, a candidate attempts 20 questions and scores 72 marks. If 5 marks are awarded for each correct answer and 2 marks are deducted for each wrong answer, then how many questions were answered correctly by him?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, 16. The candidate attempts 20 questions, so if c of them are right then 20 − c are wrong; nothing is left unattempted. Score is 5c − 2(20 − c) = 72. Expanding gives 5c − 40 + 2c = 72, so 7c = 112 and c = 16. Check it: 16 right earns 80, the remaining 4 wrong cost 8, and 80 − 8 = 72. There is a faster route for the hall. If every one of the 20 were right the score would be 100, and each question moved from right to wrong costs 5 marks gained plus 2 marks deducted, that is 7 marks. The shortfall is 100 − 72 = 28, and 28 ÷ 7 = 4 wrong answers, leaving 16 correct.

question: Which one of the following is the greatest number by which the product of three consecutive even numbers would be exactly divisible?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, 48. Write the three consecutive even numbers as 2n, 2n + 2 and 2n + 4, where n is a positive integer. Their product is 2n × 2(n + 1) × 2(n + 2) = 8 × n(n + 1)(n + 2). Now n(n + 1)(n + 2) is a product of three consecutive integers, and among any three consecutive integers one is a multiple of 3 and at least one is even, so that product is always divisible by 6. The whole expression is therefore always divisible by 8 × 6 = 48. To see that nothing larger works, take the smallest case: 2 × 4 × 6 = 48 itself, which no number above 48 can divide. So 48 divides every such product and is the greatest number that does.

question: If 15% of A is double of 30% of B, then what is the ratio of A to B?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, 4 : 1. Turn the sentence into an equation exactly as written: fifteen per cent of A is double thirty per cent of B, so 0.15A = 2 × 0.30B, that is 0.15A = 0.60B. Divide both sides by 0.15 and A = 4B, so A : B = 4 : 1. The same thing in fractions avoids decimals altogether: (15/100)A = 2 × (30/100)B gives 15A = 60B, and dividing by 15 gives A = 4B. A quick sanity check with numbers seals it: put B = 1 and A = 4; thirty per cent of 1 is 0.3, double that is 0.6, and fifteen per cent of 4 is also 0.6.

question: The cost of gold varies directly as the cube of its weight. A gold piece weighing 20 decigram costs ₹1,000. If it is broken into two pieces whose weights are in the ratio 2 : 3, then what is the profit or loss incurred?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: D, ₹720 loss. Cost varies as the cube of weight, so cost = k × weight³. From the whole piece, 1000 = k × 20³ = 8000k, giving k = 0.125. Broken in the ratio 2 : 3, the twenty decigrams split into 8 and 12. The two pieces are then worth 0.125 × 8³ = 0.125 × 512 = ₹64 and 0.125 × 12³ = 0.125 × 1728 = ₹216, a total of ₹280. The whole piece was worth ₹1,000, so breaking it destroys 1000 − 280 = ₹720 of value, which is a loss. There is a shortcut that skips k entirely: the pieces are 2/5 and 3/5 of the weight, so their values are (2/5)³ + (3/5)³ = (8 + 27)/125 = 35/125 = 7/25 of the original, and 7/25 of ₹1,000 is ₹280.

question: The average age of the boys in a class is 12 years. The average age of the girls in the class is 11 years. There are 50% more girls than boys in the class. Which one of the following is the average age of the class (in years)?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, 11.4 years. Only the ratio of boys to girls matters, so take the smallest convenient numbers. Let there be 2 boys; fifty per cent more girls than boys means 3 girls. Total age of the boys is 2 × 12 = 24 years and of the girls 3 × 11 = 33 years, so the class totals 57 years across 5 children. The average is 57 ÷ 5 = 11.4 years. The general working gives the same thing: with b boys and 1.5b girls, total age is 12b + 11 × 1.5b = 12b + 16.5b = 28.5b over 2.5b students, and 28.5 ÷ 2.5 = 11.4. The answer must lie between 11 and 12 and closer to 11, because the girls outnumber the boys, which alone rules out two of the four options.

question: A sum triples in ten years under compound interest at a certain rate of interest, the interest is being compounded annually. In how many years, it would become nine times?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, 20 years. Under annual compounding a sum multiplies by the same factor in every equal stretch of time. Ten years turns the principal into three times itself, so the ten-year growth factor is 3. Another ten years multiplies by 3 again, giving 9 times the principal after twenty years. Written out, if the annual factor is r then r¹⁰ = 3, and nine times means r^t = 9 = 3² = (r¹⁰)² = r²⁰, so t = 20. The rate itself is never needed. The general rule worth carrying is that under compound interest a sum that becomes x times in n years becomes x^k times in kn years, so trebling in ten years means nine times in twenty and twenty-seven times in thirty.

question: The number of ways by which 6 distinct balls can be put in 5 distinct boxes are
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, 15625. Both the balls and the boxes are distinct, and nothing forbids a box from holding several balls or none. Take the balls one at a time: the first can go into any of the 5 boxes, and so can the second, the third and each of the rest, with no interference between the choices. Six independent choices from 5 possibilities each give 5 × 5 × 5 × 5 × 5 × 5 = 5⁶ = 15,625. The direction of the exponent is what the item is really testing. It is balls choosing boxes, not boxes choosing balls, because every ball must go somewhere while a box may stay empty, so the count is (number of boxes) raised to the (number of balls), and 5⁶ rather than 6⁵.

question: A wire of length 6 m is stretched such that its radius is reduced by 20%. Which one of the following is the value of increase in its length?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: B, 56.25%. Stretching a wire does not change the amount of metal in it, so the volume is constant. Volume is π r² L, so r² L stays fixed. The radius falls by twenty per cent, leaving 0.8r, and the cross-sectional area therefore falls to 0.8² = 0.64 of what it was. For the product to be unchanged, the length must rise by the reciprocal: L' = L ÷ 0.64 = 1.5625L. That is an increase of 0.5625, which is 56.25 per cent. The six metres in the stem is not needed at all: the answer is a percentage, so the original length cancels; putting it in gives 6 ÷ 0.64 = 9.375 metres, an increase of 3.375 metres, and 3.375 ÷ 6 is again 56.25 per cent.

question: The alphabets from A to J are numbered from 0 to 9 respectively. Which one of the following is the value of AGJ – CEG + EDB?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, CFE. The letters run A to J against the digits 0 to 9, so A is 0, B is 1, C is 2, D is 3, E is 4, F is 5, G is 6, H is 7, I is 8 and J is 9. Translate each three-letter block into the number it stands for. AGJ becomes 0, 6, 9, that is 69. CEG becomes 2, 4, 6, that is 246. EDB becomes 4, 3, 1, that is 431. Now do the arithmetic in the order written: 69 − 246 = −177, and −177 + 431 = 254. Turn 254 back into letters, digit by digit: 2 is C, 5 is F and 4 is E, giving CFE. The leading A in AGJ is the place where candidates slip, because A stands for zero and the block is worth 69, not 690 or anything larger.

question: A is the smallest positive integer which when divided by 9 and 12 leaves remainder 8. B is the smallest positive integer which when divided by 9 and 12 leaves remainder 5. Which one of the following is the value of A – B?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: A, 3. Take A first. A number that leaves remainder 8 on division by 9 and also by 12 must be of the form 36k + 8, because 36 is the lowest common multiple of 9 and 12 and the remainder is common to both. The smallest positive value is at k = 0, which gives A = 8, and 8 does satisfy the condition, since dividing 8 by 9 leaves 8 and dividing 8 by 12 also leaves 8. By the same reasoning B is of the form 36k + 5 and the smallest positive value is B = 5. So A − B = 8 − 5 = 3. The answer is the same even for a candidate who insists on taking the next value up: 44 − 41 is also 3, because both numbers move by the same lowest common multiple. The difference of the two remainders is what survives, whichever pair is chosen.

question: If South-east is called East, North-west is called West, South-west is called South and so-on, what will North be called?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, North-west. Put the eight compass points on a dial, measuring clockwise from north: north 0, north-east 45, east 90, south-east 135, south 180, south-west 225, west 270, north-west 315. Now read the three examples the stem gives. South-east, at 135, is called east, which sits at 90. North-west, at 315, is called west, at 270. South-west, at 225, is called south, at 180. Every one of them drops by exactly 45 degrees, so the rule is that each direction takes the name of the point 45 degrees anticlockwise of itself. Apply it to north, at 0 or equivalently 360: 360 minus 45 is 315, which is north-west. So under this scheme north is called north-west.

question: If the day before yesterday was Tuesday, when will Saturday be?
source_explanation_raw: Correct: C, Day after tomorrow. Anchor on today and count outwards. The day before yesterday was Tuesday, so yesterday was Wednesday and today is Thursday. Counting forward from Thursday: tomorrow is Friday, and the day after tomorrow is Saturday. So Saturday falls on the day after tomorrow. The reliable method is to write the run of days once (Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday, Saturday) and mark today's position in it, rather than trying to hold the offsets in your head. question: In a group of 100 children, 64 children like to play cricket, 53 children like to play football and 20 children like to play both cricket and football. How many children do NOT like to play cricket or football?

question: Two years ago, the age of A was three times the age of B. If B is currently 9 years old, then after how many years, the age of A will be double of the age of B?

A was then three times that, which is 21, so A is 21 + 2 = 23 now. Let t be the number of years after which A is twice B. Then 23 + t = 2(9 + t), which expands to 23 + t = 18 + 2t, giving t = 5.
